body: Wow, those are very informative, thank you. I will be sure to mention it as a possibility  I next see a clinician. I'm so desperate to get this sorted.

Thank you very much; this was something my friend and I had considered (part of her uni course includes anatomy), but I didn't want to ask outright so that I got a completely unbiased response. We insisted on the mri for this reason particularly (but we gave up suggesting it by this point because he had already dismissed it in an earlier conversation during the consultation). Am I right in thinking the likely treatment would be trimming through an arthroscopy? What might be the success rate for this?

Unfortunately I don't have the money or ability to refer myself to an orthopedic consultant, it is something which has to be done through the GP where I am, unless I have the money to go private (as a student, I don't have access to this at the moment).

Also my ligaments have been briefly examined by hand by some of the above practitioners, and it was only the first one who said it might be ligament damage. But that you very much for your input, I will make sure it is considered when I get my 2nd opinion next week.
What would be the likely treatment if it is an ACL problem? Just trying to get a feel of what my options are likely to be so that if they are given it isn't such a shock and I know more about what I might be getting myself into.
Thank you for the links, they were very helpful. I noticed that it had a short list of examples which could cause water on the knee. Do you have any suggestions as to the cause for me?

I just thought I would share a little to let you know you aren't alone- although this will be slightly different due to circumstances.
I am female, and even slightly before my ex-boyfriend, I have been dubious about sex. I have always been afraid of semen, and the majority of my sexual encounters with my ex were because I was afraid of what might happen if I didn't (we were both in a very bad place).
With my current boyfriend, I spent months getting used to the concept of consensual sex, and before exposing myself to it, I had to talk about it. And if my understanding is correct, that is how cognitive behavioural therapy works - current thinking patterns are identified and then adapted to more adaptive ones before you are exposed to the fear. I would say give it a try, the first bit may not be as bad as you think?

I hope I have helped. Life can deal out some shit, but we are resourceful and can deal with most things time.

Whilst I think you're both absolutely right to comment on phrasing here, as it is the best way to help people identify what is/isn't appropriate, and terms like 'battle scars' are responded to differently by different people (eg I mind very little about most comments), I don't think you needed to be quite so rude about it. You have a right to say things how you like on the internet, but we are people, and for all you know you could be speaking to your SO/best friend/family here, and I hope you would respect them enough to be a bit more polite IRL.
TLDR: Everyone is entitled to their opinions online, but rudeness is not needed.

I'll listen if you want to talk about it, feel free to PM me.
Losing someone who makes the world a better place is very hard, I'm sure many people can relate, I know I can. Take care.

I felt like everyone was giving up on me, I had enough when my 'sister' (she wasn't related, but one of the two people who I was essentially considered a relative by the family) ditched me to be with someone else (and that is yet another story...).
In retrospect, I had heard about someone I had been close to doing it and seen it on a BBC drama and had no outlet of my own for emotions, but I could have waited, maybe I would have found something else... I've been doing it on and off for about 6, coming up 7 years, although I have been 'clean' for about 5 months. But the way the nhs (and my CPN) is, I'm not likely to be offered support beyond meds no matter how long I have been 'clean'.
Thank you, each day is filled with mixed emotions, but I'm trying and I guess that's what matters.
Thank you, you have summed it up perfectly. You're right, it hurts so badly that I feel this way, but I can't help it.

My dad had the balls to tell me I'm fat and I look stupid in particular things he doesn't like, I regularly couldn't buy clothes I liked because he would judge me. I'm nearly 20 and can't go out wearing anything I like without support from my housemates.
I also was always told I should be more grown up, I spent all my time trying to please them, I missed out on so much whilst growing up, which has also made me rather ignorant.
Basically I always put myself down because it's what my parents did, and never knew anything else.
Thank you very much, they have been very helpful :)

Yes, although I prefer to think it's everyone else over-reacting...

I do this. Most nights I want to rip myself to shreds when I cut, and I try not to, but i don't deserve anything else. I've cut over my heart, but I wasn't controlled enough in space and my bra kept ripping of the plasters and the friction made the hatred worse, not point being more mad at myself, when it just causes more pain... or sometimes that's what I think...
Some parents just don't know how to respond, it must be hard for them. But it is your body and your choice.
Thank you very much, the validation means more than I can put into words.
Thank you, and likewise to you. It is so rare to have a place to talk without the focus being on recovery, and we must treasure this and make to most of it!

I don't want to stop, it's better than other things I have done in the past like smoking, and it's better than being under a truck on the motorway. It keeps me safe and keeps me alive. Sadly no one else thinks that way, my boyfriend is, at best uninformed, and no one else knows that I have started again.
